full_judgment:
Mohi Uddin Shamim, J: This Rule was issued at the instance of the applicant-petitioner calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the Order No.4 dated 29-1-2023 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No.383 of 2021 appointing arbitrator for the petitioner, thereby effectively terminating the mandate of the arbitrator appointed by the petitioner should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. At the time of issuance of Rule, this Court stayed operation of the impugned order No.4 dated 29-1-2023 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 383 of 2021 and all further proceedings of Arbitration Tribunal comprising with the, pro-forma respondent formed pursuant to impugned order No.4 for a period of 3 months from date. 

 3. The salient facts leading to disposal of the Rule in short, are that the present petitioner as applicant filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No.383 of 2021 under section 12 of the. Arbitration Act, 2001 before the Court of the learned District Judge, Dhaka as per term of the agreement dated 26-12-2018 executed by the petitioner and the opposite party No.1, seeking following reliefs; 

 4. The present opposite party No.1 who was also made opposite party (with another) to the said Arbitration Miscellaneous Case entered appearance in the said Miscellaneous Case and filed written objection denying all the material averments so made in the petition for arbitration and finally prayed for rejecting the application vis-a-vis dismissing the Miscellaneous application. 

 5. That after hearing the parties learned District Judge, Dhaka vide order dated 29-1-2023 disposed of the said Miscellaneous application giving appointment to one Mrs. Tanjina Ismail, retired District and Sessions Judge, House No.62, Flat - 5/C, Judges Goli, RK Mission Road, Dhaka as Arbitrator for the petitioner and Advocate Bilkis Nasima Rahman, Chamber: Dhaka Legal Practice, 102 Kakrail Road, Ground Floor, Kakrail, Dhaka as the Arbitrator for the opposite party No.1. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 29-1-2023, the petitioner of the said Arbitration Miscellaneous Case as petitioner filed this present Civil Revision Application before this Court and obtained the instant Rule and stay. 

 8. The learned Counsel further submits that, the learned District Judge, Dhaka miserably failed to appreciate the scale, scope and spirit of the provisions of Arbitration Act, 2001, where preference of choice of the parties concerned should be given effect first unless impartiality and credibility of an Arbitrator nominated/appointed by one party is questioned by the other. But in the instant case, though the opposite party has never raised any question, whatsoever, regarding the proficiency, integrity, honesty and trustworthiness of Dr. Khaled Hamid Chowdhury, nominated and appointed by the petitioner, even then the learned District Judge changed him and gave appointment to another person going beyond the scope and spirits of law and thereby committed an error of law which occasioned failure of justice. 

 9. On the other hand, Mr MM Shofiullah, the learned advocate appearing for the opposite party No.1 by filling an application for disposing off the rule issued in, Civil Revision No.819 of 2023 by setting aside the Order No.4 dated 29-1-2023 passed by learned District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No.383 of 2021 and submits that, since the opposite party No.1 filed money suit being Money Suit No.68 of 2019 against the petitioner and he (opposite party No.1) informed the same to the petitioner in response to the arbitration Notice. The opposite party No.1 further by filing a supplementary-affidavit to the application submits that the learned District Judge by the impugned order has appointed Advocate Bilkis Nasima Rahman, Chamber: Dhaka Legal Practice, 102 Kakrail Road, Ground Floor, Kakrail, Dhaka as Arbitrator for the opposite party, however, the opposite party No.1 has no confidence upon the said arbitrator appointed by the District Judge and the opposite party no.1 is not willing to proceed with the arbitration proceeding before the tribunal consisting of Advocate Bilkis Nasima Rahman as of its Arbitrator. The learned counsel next submits that Advocate Bilkis Nasima Rahman has been enrolled as an Advocate of the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh on 15-4-2019 and the Arbitrator proposed by the petitioner namely, Dr. Khaled Hamid Chowdhury, FCI, Arb, LLD, Barrister-at-Law is a senior member of the Supreme Court Bar Association, who was enrolled as an advocate of the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh on 7-3-1996. So the Arbitrator appointed for the opposite party No.1 is no way match with the Arbitrator so appointed by the petitioner and no way she got such potentials to protect the interest of the opposite party No.1 against the arbitrator appointed for the petitioner. Learned counsel further contends that he has no objection if the dispute in question is resolved through arbitration. He categorically stated that, since party autonomy is the core essence of arbitration proceedings, therefore, he has no objection if the impugned order is set-aside and the proposed arbitrator of the petitioner namely Mr Khaled Hamid Chowdhury is replaced in the place of Mrs. Tanjila Islam, Retd. District and Sessions Judge and accept the nomination of Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, Senior Advocate, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, Chamber-46, Bir Uttam CR Dutta Road (1st Floor), 33/1/1, Sonar Gaon Road, Hatirpool, Dhaka as Arbitrator nominated and appointed by the opposite party No.1. 

 12. To adjudicate the issue, we have very meticulously gone through the order impugned in the instant Civil Revision and find that, the learned District Judge disposed of the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case by giving appointment to Mrs. Tanjina Ismail, District and Sessions Judge (Retd), as Arbitrator for the petitioner, replacing Dr. Khaled Hamid Chowdhury, FCI Arb, LLD, Barrister-at-Law, Advocate, Supreme Court of Bangladesh nominated and appointed by the petitioner without assigning any reason whatsoever. However, on plain reading of section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 we find that, there is no scope for District Judge to change the name of an Arbitrator nominated/appointed by any party, unless otherwise impartiality and credibility of an Arbitrator nominated/ appointed by one party is questioned by the other. The terms of the Rule are specific, calling in question of the appointment of the Arbitrator by the learned District Judge in place of the arbitrator nominated and appointed by the petitioner. Now, let us study section 12 of The Act, 2001; 

 14. Now, let us turn our eyes to the appointment of Arbitrator as prayed for by the opposite party No.1 by filing application and supplementary application. In this regard, we observed that the learned District Judge has rightly appointed arbitrator for the opposite party No.1 within his authority under the provisions of concerned law. The Opposite Party No.1 had waived his right to nominate and appoint arbitrator by their own choice pursuant to section 12 of the Arbitration Act as well as universal principle of "party autonomy" by not responding to the Arbitration Notice served upon them by the petitioner under section 12 of the Act. Since the petitioner failed to respond to the aforesaid Notice and contest the subsequent Arbitration Miscellaneous Case, therefore, it is the District judge who has the authority, as per law, to appoint arbitrator for the opposite party. At this juncture, the opposite party has no opportunity and right of claim the benefit of the principle of 'party autonomy'. 

 15. Though the learned District Judge has absolute authority to appoint arbitrator for the opposite party no. 1, but implementation of the authority should be rational, justified and bona fide. In the instant case, the learned District Judge appointed Advocate Ms Bilkis Nasima Rahman as the arbitrator for the opposite party No. 1, who has got permission to practice as an Advocate to the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh on 15-4-2019, while the Arbitrator proposed by the petitioner namely, Dr. Khaled Hamid Chowdhury, FCI Arb, LLD, Barrister-at-Law is a senior member of the Supreme Court Bar Association, who was enrolled as an advocate of the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh on 7-3-1996. So the appointment of Arbitrator for the opposite party is not rational and justified. 

 16. So considering the facts and circumstances of the case, and the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the contending parties, and after perusing the documents, we are of view that, justice would be best served, if, we dispose of the case by setting aside the impugned judgment and order dated 29-1-2023, passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka, in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No.383 of 2021 and return the case on remand for proper and effective adjudication of the matter. 

 20. Learned District Judge, Dhaka is also, hereby, directed to dispose of the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No.383 of 2021, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within 1 (one) months from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment.
